lessons.title: Test a seeded shuffle
objectives: Separate the value distribution from temporal order.
Repeat an experiment with the same seed.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Run one shuffle with seed 3 and sort a copy of the result.
Repeat seed 3 and compare the complete output.
Change the seed and explain why pointwise comparisons no longer describe the original chronology.
expected: The sorted result is exactly 1 through 8 and x stays 0 through 7.
Seed 3 repeats the same nonidentity ordering.
pitfalls: The browser random sequence is not Java Collections.shuffle.
Shuffled values no longer have their original event positions.

lessons.title: Scale a series by its maximum
objectives: Compute a maximum-based scale factor.
Distinguish per-series scaling from a shared physical unit.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Divide the four values by 8 before running.
Compare each prediction with the output.
Try an all-zero series and inspect the undefined division.
expected: The output is 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1 on the same coordinates.
The transform scales each series separately.
pitfalls: Zero maxima produce nonfinite values.
Maximum normalization is not z-score normalization.

lessons.title: Use sample standard deviation in a z-score
objectives: Recognize sample rather than population standard deviation.
Explain constant-series handling.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Calculate mean 0 and sample standard deviation 1.
Run the transform and verify all three values.
Replace the input by three equal values and explain the zero result.
expected: The starter remains -1, 0, 1.
A constant finite series becomes zero because the divisor falls back to 1.
pitfalls: The sample denominator is n minus 1.
The displayed unit metadata is retained even though z-scores are dimensionless.

lessons.title: Track coordinates when logarithms remove points
objectives: Identify the domain of the natural logarithm.
Track which original coordinates survive filtering.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Predict which of the four input points have finite logarithms.
Run Log and compare x and y, not only the output length.
Explain why this result cannot be treated as a regularly sampled sequence without checking x.
expected: Only coordinates 0 and 3 remain.
Their values are 0 and 1.
pitfalls: Zero and negative inputs are dropped rather than converted to gaps.
The operation can make a regular time grid irregular.

lessons.title: Measure multiplicative changes with log returns
objectives: Relate equal ratios to equal log returns.
Account for the initialized first return.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Compute the ratio of each value to its predecessor.
Predict three copies of ln(2) after the initial zero.
Compare this output with ordinary differences on the same input.
expected: The first output is 0.
Every following output is ln(2), approximately 0.69314718056.
pitfalls: Inputs must be positive to obtain finite log differences.
The first zero is an initialization convention, not an observed return.

lessons.title: Measure additive first differences
objectives: Distinguish additive differences from relative changes.
Explain the first-value convention.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Subtract each value from its successor by hand.
Run Diffs and verify the retained four coordinates.
Compare the increasing differences with the constant log returns.
expected: The output is 0, 1, 2, 4.
The original coordinate count is retained.
pitfalls: The initial zero is synthetic.
A missing input affects its own and the following difference.

lessons.title: Integrate deviations from the mean
objectives: Build a cumulative centered profile.
Understand the finite-value mean used at gaps.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Compute the mean 2 and deviations -1, 0, 1.
Accumulate them to -1, -1, 0.
Insert a gap and inspect its zero contribution after centering.
expected: The profile is -1, -1, 0.
The last value is zero for this complete finite series.
pitfalls: This is a centered cumulative sum, not a raw integral.
A gap contributes the mean before centering, so it adds zero.

lessons.title: Locate a sine in an amplitude spectrum
objectives: Relate sample spacing to frequency in hertz.
Interpret the one-sided amplitude spectrum.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Use the 0.25-second sampling interval to derive a 4 Hz sampling rate.
Predict a unit-amplitude peak at 1 Hz.
Change the signal length to inspect zero padding and explain that interpolation does not add observations.
expected: Four bins appear at 0, 0.5, 1 and 1.5 Hz.
The 1 Hz amplitude is 1; the other starter bins are zero within numerical tolerance.
pitfalls: The mean is removed before the transform.
The Nyquist endpoint is omitted and gaps are replaced by zero after centering.

lessons.title: Count values in a normalized histogram
objectives: Read bin centers separately from bin edges.
Check probability normalization.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Place 0 and 1 in the first bin and 2 and 3 in the second.
Predict the centers 1 and 3 and frequencies 0.5 each.
Add an out-of-range value and explain why it does not increase the histogram denominator.
expected: The value axis is [1, 3].
Relative frequencies sum to 1.
pitfalls: Only finite values inside the inclusive min/max range enter the denominator.
The upper endpoint belongs to the final bin.

lessons.title: Compare distributions in separate time slices
objectives: Pool series within each sample slice.
Distinguish cross-cut histograms from one histogram per series.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Pool the first two samples from both series.
Predict one all-low and one all-high histogram.
Increase the slice width to combine both distributions.
expected: Two output series represent the two slices.
Their frequencies are [1,0] and [0,1].
pitfalls: Window is a number of samples, not elapsed seconds.
Only the first 16 slices are drawn.

The native Swing action uses legacy raw counts and positive integer windows; starts follow the nonempty first series while every series contributes available samples within each nominal window. This browser workload does not establish native output parity.

lessons.title: Accumulate histogram probabilities into a CDF
objectives: Read a binned cumulative distribution.
Check its monotone endpoint.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Find the observed range from 0 to 3.
Predict two bin centers and cumulative frequencies.
Compare with Histogram and explain the extra accumulation.
expected: Bin centers are 0.75 and 2.25.
Cumulative probabilities are 0.5 and 1.
pitfalls: The operator derives its range independently for each series.
A binned CDF is not an exact empirical step function at every observation.

lessons.title: Predict entropy for balanced and partial windows
objectives: Interpret Shannon entropy in bits.
Account for partial windows near the tail.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Count the two equally likely symbols in the first four samples.
Predict 1 bit, then the entropy of probabilities 1/3 and 2/3.
Inspect why the last two samples still produce an output.
expected: Window-start coordinates are 0, 1 and 2.
Entropy values are 1, approximately 0.91829583405 and 1 bit.
pitfalls: The bin range is derived from the whole input series.

The native ENTROPY action uses maximum normalization and modulo-100 discretization within each slice, validates finite matching samples and positive integer lengths, and clips cuts to available data. This browser workload does not establish native output parity.

lessons.title: Find alternating dependence with autocorrelation
objectives: Interpret zero lag and one-sample lag.
Recognize the finite-length normalization.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Center the alternating starter, whose mean is zero.
Predict zero-lag correlation 1 and one-lag correlation -3/4.
Explain why the output axis is a lag index rather than time.
expected: The lag axis is [0,1].
Correlations are 1 and -0.75.
pitfalls: The number of returned lags is capped at floor(n/2).
Gaps can propagate through the correlation sums; they are not pairwise deleted.

lessons.title: Check a white-noise DFA exponent
objectives: Interpret the slope of log fluctuation over log scale.
Use deterministic white noise as a scaling sanity check.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Generate 8192 centered uniform samples with Mulberry32 seed 42.
Run second-order DFA over 30 requested scales.
Read alpha and compare it with the white-noise reference interval (0.4,0.6).
expected: The output is a finite increasing log-scale curve with at least 20 points.
The displayed exponent lies strictly between 0.4 and 0.6.
pitfalls: The exponent is a scaling estimate, not a causal relationship.
Short or constant data can yield too few nonzero fluctuations for an exponent.

lessons.title: Measure overlap before interpreting a pair statistic
objectives: Distinguish total ticks from jointly observed ticks.
Use coverage to qualify later pair results.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Put both inputs onto a one-second clock.
Count three jointly present ticks out of four.
Raise minCoverage above 0.75 and inspect the retained timestamp with a missing result.
expected: Coverage is 0.75 and ticks is 4.
The episode-wide result is stamped at its center, second 2.
pitfalls: A low-coverage item stays on the regular output grid as a gap.
Coverage measures available overlap, not statistical dependence.

lessons.title: Interpret a signed cross-correlation peak
objectives: Connect zero-lag Pearson correlation with the peak field.
Separate correlation, lag and strength.
Distinguish browser execution, the native Wayang mapping and frozen catalog membership.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Predict perfect correlation between the identical starter series.
Run a one-tick lag search and verify peak 1 at lag 0.
Delay B and inspect the positive lag convention that means B follows A.
Resolve pair.xcorr version 1 in the frozen inventory and compare the referenced native Wayang regression with the browser workload.
Inspect the window text field and YAML exporter; keep catalog window values as text while recognizing numeric seconds in direct pair APIs.
expected: The max field is 1 and lag is 0 seconds at center second 4.
Strength is 2/sqrt(3), approximately 1.15470053838.
pitfalls: An anticorrelated extreme can be the selected peak with a negative sign.
A single searched lag has undefined strength because there is no spread.
An available native mapping does not establish full A4 compilation or deployment through the workbench.

lessons.title: Compare event synchronization with its surrogate baseline
objectives: Detect strict local peaks above a population-deviation threshold.
Compare observed synchronization with an interval-shuffle control.
Distinguish native sampled-series Wayang execution from event-list kernel checks and deployed DAG bindings.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Predict events at ticks 1 and 4 in both inputs.
Explain why simultaneous events split equally between q_ab and q_ba.
Observe that shuffling the single inter-event interval cannot change this two-event control.
Inspect the four shared sampled-series cases through TsxPair, including state restored between B and a later A increment.
Compare largeSeedsUseTheSameUnsigned32BitStateAsTheWorkbench and settingsLabelsKeepWorkbenchNumberFormatting with the workbench settings.
Resolve pair.es version 1 in the frozen inventory and explain why native availability remains separate from full A4 compilation and deployment.
expected: q_total and q_rand are both 1.
q_ab and q_ba are both 0.5 at center second 3.
Four sampled-series vector cases match all four fields through Wayang within 5e-13, in one plan and after restoring state between increments.
The four event-list-only cases remain numerical kernel checks; TsxPairEsVectorsTest covers all eight cases.
Native random state uses the seed modulo 2^32, while sigma, tauMax, shuffles and seed labels retain workbench number formatting.
pitfalls: A large q_total alone does not prove coupling when q_rand is equally large.
First and last samples cannot be detected local-maximum events.
The frozen pair.es entry identifies native Wayang availability; it does not establish a deployed UI DAG binding or full A4 compiler support.
A large whole-number seed must wrap to the unsigned 32-bit random state without changing its settings label.

lessons.title: Calculate a cross-series sample sigma band

Separate index-wise aggregation from timestamp alignment.
prerequisites: Read x as an ordered coordinate and null as a missing value.
Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Compute the two column means, 2 and 4.
Use sample standard deviations sqrt(2) and 2sqrt(2) for the band.
Try mismatched x coordinates and explain why a separate alignment step is necessary.
expected: The three output series are mean, mean plus sigma and mean minus sigma.
Their starter values match the two hand-calculated columns.
pitfalls: Columns are paired by array position and truncated to the shortest series.
The band is a spread across input series, not a confidence interval.

lessons.title: Select a series with a case-insensitive pattern

lessons.title: Keep the clock while marking implausible values as gaps

Compare gap and clip preparation modes.

lessons.title: Aggregate a regular series into two-second windows
objectives: Read half-open aggregation windows.

lessons.title: Estimate wind at a different height

Label a model estimate separately from a measurement.

lessons.title: Check power-curve boundaries and model limits

The curve estimates potential power and does not model curtailment or measured production.

lessons.title: Build a two-sample lag without inventing history

lessons.title: Use an open-left trailing time window

lessons.title: Put two components on one clock without filling missing data

Distinguish any from complete emission and optional as-of fill.

Load the synthetic bucket and set every starter parameter explicitly.
tasks: Connect the wind and power buckets with the same series ID.
Predict three one-second ticks and a missing power value at t=1.

Lateness configures the running processor and does not delay this batch apply call.
